newsitem.title: THAILAND: Thai rubber up on tight supply, positive news.
newsitem.headline: Thai rubber up on tight supply, positive news.

text.p: Thai rubber prices were mostly firmer from last week, buoyed by tighter supply, buying interest from China and other positive news, trade sources said on Wednesday.
"News on growth of Japan's vehicle production and Japan's possible sales of Thai rubber to China helped boost the market," said one trader in Hat Yai, Thailand's major rubber trading center.
Japan's vehicle production in September rose 7.3 percent to 923,320 units.
There was also market talk last week that some Japanese traders were considering re-exporting Thai rubber to China to get rid of their stocks.
Many see prices edging up further next week.
Thai benchmark RSS3 for December shipment was quoted around $1.24-1.26 a kg FOB Bangkok, against $1.23-1.25 on Friday.
STR20 for the same shipment was quoted around $1.24 from $1.22 late last week. But latex was barely changed at 95 cents on the same FOB basis.
"On the supply side, rains continue to reduce the amount of rubber entering the market. That should support the prices too," a trader said.
Traders said China showed strong buying interest this week but some doubted whether actual buying would be substantial.

"There's strong buying interest from China, but we tend to be cautious about orders from China due to bad records of letter of credit. Thai traders usually deal with regular customers only," said another trader.
